# Loading and Cleaning
## Load And Clean

```{python}
# | label: load_data
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.dates as mdates

# Load the already merged and cleaned modeling dataset
df_combined = pd.read_csv("data/final_data.csv")

# Ensure Sold Date is datetime
df_combined["Sold Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df_combined["Sold Date"])

print(f"Total Cleaned Sales Loaded: {len(df_combined)}")

```

# Adjust Prices & Create Time Variables

## Adjust Prices

```{python}
# | label: unified_price_adjustment
# | message: false
# | warning: false

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import pwlf
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# Initialization and Transformations
df_combined["Adj_Price"] = df_combined["Sold Price"] - df_combined[
    "Concessions Amount"
].fillna(0)
df_combined = df_combined[df_combined["Adj_Price"] > 0].copy()
df_combined["ln_Price"] = np.log(df_combined["Adj_Price"])

# Handle GLA zeros before logging to avoid -inf values
df_combined["ln_GLA"] = np.log(df_combined["Total SqFt"].replace(0, np.nan))

# Timeline and Knot Selection
start_date = pd.Timestamp("2021-01-01")
lien_date = pd.Timestamp("2026-01-01")
x_days = (df_combined["Sold Date"] - start_date).dt.days.values

# Find 3 internal knots (4 segments)
pw_model = pwlf.PiecewiseLinFit(x_days, df_combined["ln_Price"].values)
knots_days = pw_model.fit(3)
knot_dates = [start_date + pd.Timedelta(days=int(k)) for k in knots_days]

# Time Bucket Generation (Vectorized)
for i in range(len(knot_dates) - 1):
    col_name = f"Time_{i + 1}"
    start, end = knot_dates[i], knot_dates[i + 1]
    # Calculate overlap of sale date with this specific bucket
    df_combined[col_name] = df_combined["Sold Date"].apply(
        lambda x: max(0, (min(x, end) - start).days / 30.44) if pd.notna(x) else 0
    )

# Segmented Trending Loop
df_combined["Trended_Price"] = df_combined["Adj_Price"].copy()
time_cols = [c for c in df_combined.columns if c.startswith("Time_")]

for seg in ["Residential", "Multi-Family", "Land Sales"]:
    df_seg = df_combined[df_combined["segment"] == seg].copy()
    if len(df_seg) < 20:
        continue

    valid_buckets = [col for col in time_cols if df_seg[col].max() > 0]

    # Custom formula: Land Sales don't have GLA/Year Built in many datasets
    if seg != "Land Sales":
        formula = f"ln_Price ~ {' + '.join(valid_buckets)} + ln_GLA + Q('Year Built')"
        df_clean = df_seg.dropna(subset=["ln_GLA", "Year Built"])
    else:
        formula = f"ln_Price ~ {' + '.join(valid_buckets)}"
        df_clean = df_seg

    try:
        res_ols = smf.ols(formula, data=df_clean).fit()

        # Calculate the multiplier to bring the sale forward to 2026
        adj_log = 0
        for idx, col in enumerate(time_cols):
            if col in res_ols.params:
                # Max months available in this bucket
                bucket_cap = (knot_dates[idx + 1] - knot_dates[idx]).days / 30.44
                # Months remaining from sale date to the end of the bucket
                remaining = (
                    bucket_cap - df_combined.loc[df_combined["segment"] == seg, col]
                )
                adj_log += res_ols.params[col] * np.maximum(0, remaining)

        # Apply the cumulative trend to the origin segment
        df_combined.loc[df_combined["segment"] == seg, "Trended_Price"] *= np.exp(
            adj_log
        )
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Regression failed for {seg}: {e}")

print("Price Trending Complete.")
```


## Price Adustment Visual

```{python}
# | label: trend_visualization_refined
# | code-fold: true

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.dates as mdates

# Filter for Residential visualization
df_plot = df_combined[
    (df_combined["segment"] == "Residential") & (df_combined["Total SqFt"] > 100)
].copy()

# Unit Price Calculation
df_plot["Price_SqFt_Original"] = df_plot["Adj_Price"] / df_plot["Total SqFt"]
df_plot["Price_SqFt_Trended"] = df_plot["Trended_Price"] / df_plot["Total SqFt"]

# Statistical Cleaning for Plotting
y_limit = df_plot["Price_SqFt_Original"].quantile(0.98)
df_plot = df_plot[df_plot["Price_SqFt_Original"] < y_limit]
df_plot["date_num"] = mdates.date2num(df_plot["Sold Date"])

plt.figure(figsize=(16, 8))

# Volatile Original Market
sns.regplot(
    data=df_plot,
    x="date_num",
    y="Price_SqFt_Original",
    scatter_kws={"alpha": 0.1, "color": "gray", "s": 12},
    line_kws={
        "color": "#e74c3c",
        "label": "Original Market (Volatile)",
        "linewidth": 3,
    },
    lowess=True,
)

# Stabilized Trended Market
sns.regplot(
    data=df_plot,
    x="date_num",
    y="Price_SqFt_Trended",
    scatter=False,
    line_kws={
        "color": "#3498db",
        "label": f"Trended to {lien_date.date()} (Stabilized)",
        "linewidth": 4,
    },
    lowess=False,
)

# Render Inflection Knots
for s in knot_dates:
    plt.axvline(mdates.date2num(s), color="black", linestyle="--", alpha=0.2)

# Formatting
ax = plt.gca()
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b %Y"))
plt.ylim(0, y_limit)
plt.title("Residential Housing Market Stabilization", fontsize=22, pad=20)
plt.ylabel("Price per Square Foot ($)", fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel("Sale Date", fontsize=14)
plt.legend(
    loc="upper left", fontsize=13, frameon=True, facecolor="white", framealpha=0.9
)
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.15)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## MLR


```{python}
# | label: mlr
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# Filter for Residential to keep the physical coefficients meaningful
df_mlr = df_combined[df_combined["segment"] == "Residential"].copy()
df_mlr = df_mlr.dropna(subset=["Trended_Price", "Total SqFt", "Year Built", "NbhdCode"])

# Log-Linear Model Formula
formula = "np.log(Trended_Price) ~ ln_GLA + Q('Year Built') + Q('Total Bedrooms') + Q('Full Baths') + C(NbhdCode)"

# Fit the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model
model_res = smf.ols(formula, data=df_mlr).fit()

# Display the regression results
print(model_res.summary())
```

## Diagnostic Plots
```{python}
# | label: diagnostic_plots
# | fig-align: center
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as stats
import seaborn as sns

# Create a wide horizontal canvas for the two-panel layout
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 7))

# Residuals vs Fitted: Testing for Homoscedasticity
# Uses a LOWESS smoother to track the mean error trend
sns.residplot(
    x=model_res.fittedvalues,
    y=model_res.resid,
    lowess=True,
    ax=ax1,
    scatter_kws={"alpha": 0.15, "s": 25, "color": "gray"},
    line_kws={"color": "#e74c3c", "lw": 4},
)
ax1.axhline(0, color="black", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)
ax1.set_title("Residuals vs. Fitted (Error Variance)", fontsize=20, pad=15)
ax1.set_xlabel("Predicted Log Price", fontsize=14)
ax1.set_ylabel("Residual (Error)", fontsize=14)

# Normal Q-Q Plot: Testing the Gaussian assumption of OLS
# Deviations at the ends indicate 'Fat Tails' in the market data
stats.probplot(model_res.resid, dist="norm", plot=ax2)
ax2.get_lines()[0].set_markerfacecolor("gray")
ax2.get_lines()[0].set_alpha(0.15)
ax2.get_lines()[1].set_color("#3498db")
ax2.get_lines()[1].set_linewidth(4)
ax2.set_title("Normal Q-Q Plot (Error Distribution)", fontsize=20, pad=15)
ax2.set_xlabel("Theoretical Quantiles", fontsize=14)
ax2.set_ylabel("Sample Quantiles", fontsize=14)

plt.tight_layout(pad=4.0)
plt.show()
```

## Improving Model Robustness: Strategic Outlier Trimming

To address the **extreme kurtosis (351.2)** and heavy tails identified in the diagnostic plots, we applied a **statistical trim** to the data, filtering out transactions outside the typical residential market range (0.5% and 99.5% of prices).

This action removes distressed sales and extreme luxury estates, allowing the model to focus on the standard housing stock that OLS is best suited to model.

```{python}
# | label: outlier_trimming
# | echo: true
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Apply a statistical 'trim' to isolate the typical market
# Removes the most extreme 1% of transactions (0.5% on each tail)
price_lower = df_mlr['Trended_Price'].quantile(0.005)
price_upper = df_mlr['Trended_Price'].quantile(0.995)

df_trimmed = df_mlr[
    (df_mlr['Trended_Price'] > price_lower) & 
    (df_mlr['Trended_Price'] < price_upper)
].copy()

# Re-run the Log-Linear OLS Model on the cleaned dataset
formula = "np.log(Trended_Price) ~ ln_GLA + Q('Year Built') + Q('Full Baths') + C(NbhdCode)"
model_clean = smf.ols(formula, data=df_trimmed).fit()

# Define labels for the comparison table
model_stats = pd.DataFrame({
    'Metric': ['Observations', 'R-squared', 'Kurtosis', 'ln_GLA (Coef)', 'ln_GLA (P-value)'],
    'Original Model': [
        f"{model_res.nobs:.0f}", 
        f"{model_res.rsquared:.3f}", 
        "351.2", # Kurtosis from your previous output
        f"{model_res.params['ln_GLA']:.4f}",
        f"{model_res.pvalues['ln_GLA']:.4f}"
    ],
    'Trimmed Model': [
        f"{model_clean.nobs:.0f}", 
        f"{model_clean.rsquared:.3f}", 
        "Pending", # You will need to calculate this (see below)
        f"{model_clean.params['ln_GLA']:.4f}",
        f"{model_clean.pvalues['ln_GLA']:.4f}"
    ]
})

# To get the new Kurtosis number:
from scipy.stats import kurtosis
kurt_new = kurtosis(model_clean.resid, fisher=True)
print(f"New Residual Kurtosis: {kurt_new}")
```

## New Model

```{python}
# | label: trimmed_mlr_vif
# | echo: true

from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Final Trimmed Model Run
formula = "np.log(Trended_Price) ~ ln_GLA + Q('Year Built') + Q('Full Baths') + Q('Total Bedrooms')"
model_final = smf.ols(formula, data=df_trimmed).fit()

# Calculate VIF
X = model_final.model.exog
vif_data = pd.DataFrame()
vif_data["Variable"] = model_final.model.exog_names
vif_data["VIF"] = [variance_inflation_factor(X, i) for i in range(X.shape[1])]

# Filter out the Intercept and Neighborhood dummies for a cleaner view
vif_summary = vif_data[~vif_data["Variable"].str.contains("NbhdCode|Intercept")]

print(model_final.summary())
print("\n--- Variance Inflation Factors (VIF) ---")
print(vif_summary.round(2))
```

## Final

```{python}
# | label: final_consolidated_mlr

# Re-adding Neighborhoods to the formula
formula = "np.log(Trended_Price) ~ ln_GLA + Q('Year Built') + Q('Full Baths') + Q('Total Bedrooms') + C(NbhdCode)"

model_final = smf.ols(formula, data=df_trimmed).fit()

print(f"Final Observations: {model_final.nobs}")
print(f"Final R-Squared: {model_final.rsquared:.4f}")
print(model_final.summary())
```
